Given that the points $(10,6)$ and $(-6,8)$ lie on a diameter of a circle, what are the center and radius of the circle?

The circle is centered at  $(${{field-1}}$,${{field-2}}$)$ and its radius is{{field-3}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The center of the circle is located at the midpoint of the diameter. So, we can calculate the coordinates of the center using the midpoint formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}(h,k) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{10+(-6)}{2},\frac{6+8}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{4}{2},\frac{14}{2}) \\  & =(2,7)\end{aligned}
$$

The radius can be found by calculating the distance between the center $(2,7)$ and a point on the circle, such as $(10,6):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(2-10)}^{2}+{(7-6)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-8)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+1} \\  & =\sqrt{65}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(2,7),$ and its radius is $\sqrt{65}.$
